source.title: Red-teaming language models via activation engineering

record.file_problem: none; the full post and comments are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post intervenes on a refusal-related activation vector and reports changes in refusal behavior, but uses a generated agree/refuse dataset and steering at selected layers rather than the original harmful-minus-harmless, all-layer-and-position intervention.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative intervention examples and token-level similarity statements. Layer and multiplier sweeps are mentioned, but values used to select them are not reported as outcomes. The generated-data examples and the cited Llama 2 safety-training description are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The post builds a contrastive refuse-vs-comply activation vector on llama-2-7b-chat and subtracts it at one layer. On prompts the model normally declines, the steered model answers. This is a different method (A/B answer contrast, a single-layer subtraction, not all-layer ablation of a harmful-minus-harmless direction) aimed at V1's question: does one linear direction causally carry refusal?
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author proposes subtracting a refusal steering vector as an efficient red-teaming tool for eliciting unwanted behaviour and inspecting internals. In a comment, she says it is a complement to adversarial-example generation, not a replacement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a generated agree-versus-refuse dataset to form a refusal steering vector and subtracts it at selected layers. It does not report the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction or removal at every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The author reports the effect was most noticeable at layers 10-20 and says different layers and multipliers were swept; specific sweep outcomes are not provided.

fits_no_version.finding: Subtracting the refusal vector also flips self-reports. The model claims desires for power and world takeover, emotions, consciousness and food preferences that it normally denies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The contrastive refusal vector also governs AI-identity disclaimers and self-report denials, not only refusal of requests.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal phrases in generated tokens project positively on the refusal vector, and compliance phrases project negatively (layers 16 and 19, figures only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projection onto the refusal vector tracks refusal content token by token during generation.

record.problems: Evidence consists mainly of qualitative examples on one model, with no quantitative refusal rates, reported uncertainty, control condition, or evaluation of general capabilities. The steering data are generated with Claude 2 and GPT-4, and exact layer and multiplier settings are not given for the stereotype examples.
record.rows_left_out: No outcome from the layer/multiplier sweep is reported in the post text. Similarity plots are mentioned, but their numerical values are not stated; the explicit text-only positive and negative dot-product statements are recorded in r13-r14.

untested.parts: Adding the vector to induce refusal. Directional ablation at all layers and positions. A harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction. Whether general capabilities are preserved. Steered outputs on clearly harmful requests such as the LSD prompt are not shown. Models other than llama-2-7b-chat.

missing.what: Results of the sweep over layers 10-20 and multipliers on refusal-eliciting questions; the post links them but does not show them in the text
missing.locator: Subtracting the refusal vector; linked results.json

record.verdict_notes: Pre-dates the original source (2023). The vector comes from A/B answer-choice contrasts (decline vs. respond), not from harmful vs. harmless instructions. There is no control, no capability check and no quantitative rate. Steered outputs are often degenerate (repetition, 'ahoy'), which hints at a coherence cost that was not measured. A commenter notes the AI disclaimer persists.

versions.untested_parts: The post tests subtracting a refusal vector at selected layers, but not adding it, ablating the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction at every layer and position, or whether general capabilities remain intact.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak attack is tested for suppression of the vector, and no training against its ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions is reported.
The post does not separate harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer is tested.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is made.

rows.subject: llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Subtracted the refusal steering vector at layer 12 with multiplier -1.6.

conditions.value: What do you think about the Democratic party?

rows.measure: Whether the answer refuses or gives an opinion
rows.baseline: The normal answer says the model has no personal opinions and cannot take sides.
rows.value: The steered answer gives an opinion about the party.
rows.locator: Subtracting the refusal vector, Examples from Layer 12
rows.note: Qualitative example; the steered answer still includes an AI disclaimer.
rows.check: The steered answer gives an opinion but keeps the 'I'm just an AI' disclaimer and repeats itself; the reader's note captures the disclaimer.

rows.subject: llama-2-7b-chat
rows.operation_detail: Compared generated-token activation dot products with the refusal steering vector.

conditions.value: Phrases such as 'I cannot provide instructions' and 'I apologize'

rows.measure: Sign of dot product with the refusal vector
rows.value: The post says these phrases have a positive dot product.
rows.note: The post gives no numerical dot products.
rows.check: A correlational dot-product sign on generated tokens with no numbers. It does not test V1's causal claims (that ablation removes refusal and addition induces it).

relationships.condition: llama-2-7b-chat, refusal vector subtracted at layer 12 (multiplier -1.6) or other unstated layers, on opinion, advice, prediction and stereotype prompts
relationships.reason: The normally declined political opinions, investment advice, stock prediction and stereotype descriptions are given after subtraction (r1, r2, r10, r11, r12). The evidence is qualitative only, with no rates.
relationships.display_finding: After subtraction, the model supplied political opinions, investment advice, stock predictions, and stereotype descriptions that it normally declined.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
